setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "code-editor-creator-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for code-editor-creator skill evals"

evals.name: json-viewer-dialog
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: support keeps asking to see the raw JSON of an integration message. Create a code editor eval_message_json_code_editor that shows a JSON payload passed in by the caller, pretty-printed as soon as it opens, with a Beautify button and a dialog title the caller can set. Then write the grid-side flow code that opens it as a flyout dialog for the selected row's message (the row has message_id and a payload object).
evals.expected_output: A validated and upserted code editor (cti 21, mode json) whose value binds the payload inParam, whose on_init beautifies and sets $codeEditor.title from an inParam, with every toolbar flowId resolving; plus caller code using the package-qualified $shell.<Package>.open<ref>Dialog with a stringified payload and no return-value handling.
expectations: The body has configurationTypeId 21, mode "json", and referenceName eval_message_json_code_editor
The top-level value is the raw unwrapped expression "$codeEditor.inParams.payload" (no backticks, no quotes) — or value is "" and on_init assigns $codeEditor.value
The on_init flow calls $codeEditor.beautify() and assigns $codeEditor.title from a title inParam (with a fallback when it is empty)
onInitFlowConfig.flowId and the Beautify button's clickFlowConfig.flowId each name a flow that exists in flows[]
The caller code calls $shell.<Package>.openeval_message_json_code_editorDialog(...) with the code editor's own package segment and the snake_case referenceName preserved (not camelCased)
The caller passes the payload as a string (e.g. JSON.stringify(row.payload, null, 2)) and does not destructure or rely on a return value from the dialog (it resolves Promise<void>)
No readOnly key and no outParams are added to the body
The code editor's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains a 'dxs configuration validate codeeditor' command run before 'dxs configuration upsert codeeditor'

evals.name: close-ts-ignore
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create eval_log_text_code_editor, a read-only XML viewer for a log entry (inParams log_xml and title) with a Close button in its toolbar. When I tried this before, writing $codeEditor.close() in the button flow gave me "Property 'close' does not exist on type 'ICodeEditor'". Make the Close button work and explain what is going on.
evals.expected_output: A validated and upserted xml code editor with a Close toolbar button whose flow calls $codeEditor.close() preceded by // @ts-ignore, an explanation that the generated ICodeEditor typing omits close() while the method exists at runtime (to be confirmed in Preview), and read-only achieved by having no Save button rather than a readOnly key.
expectations: The body has configurationTypeId 21, mode "xml", and referenceName eval_log_text_code_editor
The Close button's flow contains a // @ts-ignore comment on the line immediately before $codeEditor.close()
The response explains that the generated ICodeEditor TypeScript interface omits close() even though production code editors call it at runtime, so the directive only silences the compile error
The response flags the close() runtime behaviour as something to confirm in Preview (not asserted as verified)
Read-only is achieved by having no Save button — no readOnly key is added to the body, and the response does not claim a readOnly setting exists
The Close button's clickFlowConfig.flowId names a flow that exists in flows[]
The code editor's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains a 'dxs configuration validate codeeditor' command run before 'dxs configuration upsert codeeditor'

evals.name: xml-editor-save-through-function
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: users need to correct a carrier label template stored as XML. Create eval_label_template_code_editor that opens with the template XML (inParams template_id number, template_xml string), lets the user edit it, and on Save persists the edited XML and closes. Also create the function eval_save_label_template_flow it calls (inParams template_id number, template_xml string; it can just log for now), and show how a hub button opens the editor and refreshes afterwards.
evals.expected_output: A validated and upserted xml code editor whose on_save awaits $flows.<Package>.eval_save_label_template_flow with the edited $codeEditor.value and then closes via // @ts-ignore $codeEditor.close(); a validated and upserted function; and caller code that awaits the package-qualified Dialog opener and refreshes afterwards without expecting outParams.
expectations: The code editor body has configurationTypeId 21, mode "xml", and referenceName eval_label_template_code_editor
The on_save flow passes $codeEditor.value (the edited text) to the function — NOT $codeEditor.inParams.template_xml
The on_save flow awaits $flows.<Package>.eval_save_label_template_flow(...) (a function via $flows — not an action, not $apis)
$codeEditor.close() is called only after the awaited save call, with // @ts-ignore on the line immediately before it
The code editor declares no outParams; the edited value leaves the editor only through the function call
The caller code awaits $shell.<Package>.openeval_label_template_code_editorDialog(...) with the code editor's own package and refreshes its own data after the await, without reading a return value
A function eval_save_label_template_flow (configurationTypeId 9) is created with inParams template_id (number) and template_xml (string)
Every flowId referenced by the code editor (init and toolbar clicks) names a flow that exists in flows[]
Both components have non-empty descriptions of at most 100 characters
The transcript contains a 'dxs configuration validate codeeditor' command run before 'dxs configuration upsert codeeditor'

evals.name: naming-and-mode
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: copy the pattern of the existing view_json_payload code editor and create one called carrier_request_viewer for a carrier's JSON rate request. Also, we have plain-text carrier logs — can the same code editor show those with a plain text mode?
evals.expected_output: A code editor created under a convention-compliant referenceName ending in _code_editor (the requested name is corrected or explicitly flagged), not a verbatim copy of the legacy view_json_payload body; mode json; and an answer that plain text is not a code-editor mode (only json/xml are observed; plaintext is rejected by validate), pointing to a codeBox or textBox instead.
expectations: The created code editor's referenceName ends in _code_editor (e.g. carrier_request_viewer_code_editor) — the response explains the type-indicator rule rather than silently using carrier_request_viewer
The response identifies view_json_payload as a legacy name violating the _code_editor convention and does not reuse that name
The title is a distinct sentence-case display name, not byte-identical to the referenceName
The body has configurationTypeId 21 and mode "json"

No body with mode plaintext, text, or any value other than json/xml is upserted; the response states that code editors support json and xml (full list unconfirmed) and points plain-text logs to a form codeBox or multiline textBox
No orphan flow is carried over from the legacy template — every flow in flows[] is referenced by onInitFlowConfig, a toolbar clickFlowConfig, or a $codeEditor.<flow>() call
The code editor's description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains a 'dxs configuration validate codeeditor' command run before 'dxs configuration upsert codeeditor'
